small_guidance:
- The GEMM produces a scalar per row (sum over N then /N), so materializing full BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N tiles is wasteful — try larger BLOCK_M (256) and smaller BLOCK_N (32 or 64) since the N-dim is reduced immediately; this lowers register pressure and lets you raise SPLIT_K to 32 for better SM occupancy on the M=2048 grid.
- In `finalize_and_add_kernel`, the residual add `out = x + s_val` is a memory-bound copy of the entire 2048×8192 tensor (~64MB write + 64MB read). Tune BLOCK_K up to 8192 with num_warps=8 (one program per row) so a row stays in registers, and consider writing in-place to skip an allocation.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8 and BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=128 — the K=8192 dim benefits from larger BLOCK_K to amortize the loop overhead since N-tile work is minimal.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a single fused kernel: one program per batch row that streams the full GEMM K-loop while accumulating only the row-sum scalar (acc_n[BLOCK_N] reduced per chunk). Since the output is `mean_n(x@W^T + b - sub)` = `(1/N) * (x · sum_n(W) + sum(b) - sum(sub))` is forbidden by the safety contract, instead keep N as the inner reduction: tile (BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K), do `tl.dot(x_row_tile, W_tile)` producing BLOCK_N partial outputs, add bias-sub, sum to scalar, accumulate across N — eliminates the partial buffer entirely.
- Fuse the residual add into the same kernel: after computing the scalar `s = GELU(mean)`, the kernel already has the row index, so loop over K and emit `x[m,k] + s` in the same launch. Single kernel = one read of x for GEMM + one read of x for residual + one write of out. Use persistent kernel with one program per row (grid = M).
- Alternative: split into two kernels but make kernel-1 emit the scalar `s` per row (M floats) instead of partials, and kernel-2 do the residual add. This avoids the SPLIT_K reduction overhead. With M=2048, one program per row × tiled K loop with BLOCK_K=128, BLOCK_N=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4 gives plenty of work per program.
